title: Surge soft-clipping profiles and layer rescale validation for LLama/Mistral/Qwen INT8/FP8
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight, model-aware soft-clipping and layer rescale validation workflow to reduce calibration-induced accuracy regressions for LLama, Mistral and Qwen families when converting to INT8 and FP8 profiles. Goal is to provide an automated per-layer profiling pass that recommends soft-clipping thresholds and multiplicative rescale corrections (applied at export time) rather than aggressive global clipping. This ticket covers: 1) collecting per-layer activation tail statistics from a representative calibration corpus, 2) computing a soft-clipping function (parametric tanh/softsign) with per-channel slope constraints, 3) deriving a minimal multiplicative rescale per-layer to preserve distribution shape post-quantization, and 4) building an automated validation harness that compares end-to-end perplexity and targeted NLU alignment tests across model variants and quant settings. The workflow should be low-latency to run in CI for model-boarding and produce human-readable recommendations for runtime policies.
acceptance_criteria: Per-layer activation statistics pipeline integrated into calibration harness and runnable as a separate job (CI and locally)
Automated computation of soft-clipping parameters and per-layer rescale factors saved as a JSON profile per model and quant scheme
Validation harness that runs end-to-end generation (5 prompts per model) and computes delta vs FP32 baselines for perplexity and two targeted metrics (answer accuracy, hallucination rate)
Regression threshold: <1.5% relative drop on accuracy suite for INT8 profiles and <1.0% for FP8 on curated workloads
Profile artifacts stored in model-catalog /profiles/<model>/<quant>-<date>.json and surfaced in the console as a suggested recommendation
Documented PR with design/usage examples and a small perf/overhead note added to runtime-1.21 release notes
tasks: Instrument activation histogram collector to capture tails at 99.7/99.9/99.99 percentiles (batch-mode and stream-mode)
Implement parametric soft-clipping candidate generator (tanh-based and piecewise-linear fallback)
Design and implement per-layer multiplicative rescale solver with L2 penalty to avoid large corrections
Add CI job that runs the calibration + validation harness for a sample of LLama, Mistral and Qwen cores
Produce profile JSON schema and serializer compatible with model-catalog ingestion
Create console UI hook (opt-in) that shows recommended profile and allows applying automatically for deploys
notes: Motivation: existing aggressive clipping reduces token-level noise but shifted distribution causes subtle ranking and generation errors on conversational prompts

Trade-offs: soft-clipping preserves tails while limiting extreme activation values; multiplicative rescale fixes layerwise gain but can interact with layernorms—we'll limit rescale to <1.25x by default
Calibration corpus: use 10k diverse tokens from production-like prompts (privacy filtered). See drive doc for seed lists: https://docs.google.com/document/d/abc123
Edge-case: Qwen attention block with rotary embeddings shows multi-modal tail; require per-head check and fall back to conservative clipping for heads flagged unstable
